newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgacom sees 1996 sales up 9 pct, higher profit.
newsitem.headline: Belgacom sees 1996 sales up 9 pct, higher profit.

text.p: Belgian state telephone company Belgacom SA said on Thursday its provisional consolidated turnover rose 9.4 percent to 139 billion francs in 1996.
It said in a statement it also expected 1996 full-year consolidated net profit rose in line with the rise in the first half of the year.
Belgacom had a 1996 first-half group net profit of 6.6 billion francs, up 15.0 percent from a year earlier.

It said in the statement the driving force behind the increase of turnover was its Belgacom Mobile subsidiary, which operates Belgium's first GSM network and the old analogue mobile phone network. Belgacom Mobile is 25 percent owned by U.S. AirTouch Communications Inc.
Belgacom Mobile had 410,172 clients by the end of 1996, against 235,238 a year earlier.
Total group investments have been scaled down to 28 billion francs, against 44 billion in 1995.
